newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat called down 3 to 5 cents on USDA data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat called down 3 to 5 cents on USDA data.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures were expected to open down three to five cents per bushel, mostly in response to a government forecast showing a jump in soft red winter wheat production, traders said.
"We know we have a big wheat crop, now we're going to have to wait and see how demand is," said one trader for a commission house.
USDA forecast Friday the 1997 soft red winter wheat crop at 455 million bushels. That figure came in above trade expectations for 405 to 440 million bushels.
A lower-than-expected USDA spring wheat production forecast of 569 million bushels was seen encouraging spreading between the Minneapolis Grain Exchange and the CBOT, traders and analysts said.
"The spring wheat number is the surprising one," said a trader. "We'll probably see some exchange spreading."
